body:
Depends on [[T-111]] (which provides the catalog and locale resolution). This is
the user-facing control and its persistence.

## Requirement (user)

A language chooser on the **login page** and in **user settings**, on **both**
clients, remembered across restarts.

## Storage: device-local, NOT synced to the account (decided)

`localStorage` on web, DataStore preferences on Android. Deliberately NOT added
to `account_settings` alongside `default_currency`/`initials`, for two reasons:

1. The login page must offer it before any account exists, so device-local
   persistence is required regardless — syncing would only ADD a second source of
   truth and a conflict rule ("you picked Arabic on the login screen, your account
   says German — which wins?").
2. Language is genuinely a device property, unlike currency (your money) or
   initials (your identity). A German phone and an English work laptop is a normal
   arrangement.

Consequence: **no server change and no wire-contract change.** A fresh device
falls back to the browser/OS locale until told otherwise.

## Behaviour

- Default = browser/OS locale, narrowed to the nearest shipped language, else `en`.
- An explicit choice pins the language and survives restart, logout and account
  switch (it is a device setting, not a session one).
- Changing it must apply immediately without a reload, on both clients — that is
  what forces the web catalog to be reactive (context + hook, not a module-level
  constant read at import) and forces Android to use a runtime locale switch
  rather than relying solely on the system locale at process start.
- Selecting Arabic must flip layout direction live — see [[T-126]].
- Language names are shown in their OWN language (Deutsch, Español, العربية,
  Українська), never translated into the current UI language. This is the
  standard convention and it is the only way a user who has accidentally
  selected a language they cannot read can get back out.

## Android note

Runtime locale switching needs either `AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales`
(pulls in appcompat, which this Compose/Material3 app does not currently depend
on) or a `CompositionLocalProvider` wrapping `LocalConfiguration` with an
overridden locale. Pick one deliberately; the second avoids a new dependency but
must be applied at the composition root so every screen and dialog inherits it,
and does not affect strings resolved outside composition (notifications,
WorkManager) — those need the locale passed or resolved separately.

The collaborator-change notification is the known case that renders outside
composition.

## Verification

- Choose a language on the login page, log in: it persists.
- Choose in settings: applies live, no reload.
- Restart the app / reload the page: choice retained.
- Log out and back in as a different account: choice retained (device setting).
- Pick Arabic: layout mirrors live.
- A language the device is set to but the app does not ship falls back to `en`,
  not to a crash or an empty string.
title: language chooser on login + settings, both clients, device-local
